newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: First forecast of Yugo 1997 wheat crop 2.8 mln T.
newsitem.headline: First forecast of Yugo 1997 wheat crop 2.8 mln T.

text.p: The first forecast of Yugoslavia's 1997 wheat harvest put production at around 2.8 million tonnes, an increase of 84 percent on last year, the Federal Statistics Office said in its latest report.
Last year's wheat harvest plunged to a 25-year low of just 1.51 million tonnes from 2.97 million tonnes in 1995.
This year's wheat acreage of 801,282 hectares was around 218,000 ha or 37 percent more than the wheat area harvested last year.
Expected yield per hectare of around 3.47 tonnes was some 890 kilograms, or 34 percent above last year's average yield.

Average yield on the 178,213 ha sown by agricultural enterprises and farm cooperatives is expected to be around 4.04 tonnes per ha, and on the 623,000 ha sown on individual farms around 3.3 tonnes per ha.
NOTES -- The Federal Statistics Office based its first forecasts on the state of the sown crop on May 10.

Having in mind the influence of weather conditions in the early stages of sprouting, ripening and during harvest, the data serves only as a rough orientation on possible wheat production this year, the office said. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
